name: Knight-Swift Transportation Holdings Inc.

profile.description: Knight-Swift is North America's largest full-truckload carrier. It runs Trucking, Logistics (brokerage), Less-than-Truckload (AAA Cooper, MME, DHE), and Intermodal segments across the U.S., Mexico, and Canada, with about 18,000 tractors and 67,600 trailers in its truckload fleet. Q3 2026 revenue was $2.2B (+14.2% YoY), with GAAP EPS of $0.72 versus $0.05 a year earlier and adjusted EPS of $0.83, as truckload rates per loaded mile rose 9.7%. CEO Adam Miller, a 22-year company veteran and former CFO, succeeded Dave Jackson. Market cap is about $10.0B.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Knight-Swift has turned itself from a pure truckload carrier into a multimodal platform by building a national LTL network through acquisitions (AAA Cooper, MME, DHE) and absorbing U.S. Xpress, which opened a new revenue stream beyond truckload [2][5]. AI Deployment (0/2): The searches found no quantified AI-driven savings or AI products. Trade press contrasts brokers such as C.H. Robinson, which reports AI paying dividends, with carriers like Knight-Swift that are focused on resilience [5]. Market Share (2/2): It is the largest full-truckload carrier in North America, with about 18,000 tractors and 67,600 trailers in its truckload fleet [3]. Product Pipeline (0/2): No named next-generation offerings with launch timelines. Growth plans are about LTL terminal expansion and rate recovery [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No disclosed R&D spend [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): The stated mission and values of safety, service, and operational excellence are boilerplate for a carrier and do not describe a purpose beyond moving freight efficiently [6]. Community Impact (0/2): The searches found no distinctive, quantified foundation or community program. Disclosures focus on emissions reduction rather than community giving [7]. Employee Retention (0/2): The company discloses no driver retention data, its 10-Ks describe wage-and-hour class actions, and trucking driver turnover is structurally high [7]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying by executives was identified in the last 12 months.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Scored mechanically as a Growth stock, since the 1.27% dividend yield is below the 2% Dividend-sleeve threshold. D/E is 36.9% (1.0). TTM ROE is just 2.2% (0.15, 2x) and TTM GAAP net margin 1.9% (0.10), reflecting losses in Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 [3]. TTM revenue grew 7.0% to $8.0B (0.90), and 5-year revenue per share grew 67% cumulatively, about a 10.8% CAGR (1.0, 2x) [3]. Forward P/E of about 15.0x is derived from the FY2027 consensus EPS of $4.10 (1.0), and the provider's forward PEG is 0.81 (1.0, 2x) [3]. Weighted sum 7.29/10 gives a score of 7. The liquidity floor is easily passed at about $209M per day.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Knight-Swift moves physical freight with about 18,000 tractors, 67,600 trailers, and a national LTL terminal network, all subject to FMCSA safety and hours-of-service rules, so AI cannot substitute for the service [3]. Autonomous Class 8 trucking is a long-term variable, but it is more likely to lower a scaled carrier's driver costs than to displace a company that owns the terminals, equipment, and shipper relationships. AI-driven brokerage gains at C.H. Robinson are a competitive pressure on Knight-Swift's logistics segment rather than its asset-based core [5]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI revenue.

infinite_game.summary: Knight-Swift is a well-run consolidator that plays the freight cycle skillfully. It invested in LTL through the 2023-2025 freight recession and promoted a 22-year insider to CEO. Its language centers on scale, cost control, safety, and financial discipline rather than a cause bigger than the company, and an unplanned CEO change during an earnings slump hints at short-term pressure. Sinek would call it a strong finite player with some infinite habits.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The stated mission of safe, reliable service and operational excellence is a corporate mission, not a vision of a better future that people would sacrifice for [6]. It does not visibly drive strategy beyond efficiency.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership kept expanding the LTL network and integrating U.S. Xpress through a multi-year freight recession that pushed GAAP earnings to losses in Q4 2025 and Q1 2026, betting on long-term network capability [2][3]. That investment is now showing up in the Q3 2026 earnings recovery [1].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Promoting Adam Miller, a 22-year veteran, to CEO shows bench depth and continuity, and the company describes his leadership style as inclusive [4]. However, the CEO change was not part of an existing transition plan and came amid falling earnings and insurance losses, and wage-and-hour litigation persists [4][7].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Moving from pure truckload into LTL, intermodal, and logistics is a real business-model evolution, which one analysis calls aggressive diversification [4][5]. It remains an incremental extension of freight transportation.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Public messaging focuses on being the largest carrier, consolidating smaller ones, and cost discipline, with no evident framing of rivals such as Old Dominion or J.B. Hunt as sources of learning [4][5].

investment_thesis: Knight-Swift's cyclical earnings recovery is under way. Q3 2026 revenue rose 14.2% to $2.2B, truckload revenue per loaded mile rose 9.7%, and adjusted EPS of $0.83 versus $0.32 beat the roughly $0.76 consensus for a third straight beat [1][2]. Management guides Q4 revenue excluding fuel up 8-11% and expects truckload growth to accelerate [2]. At $61.66 the stock trades at about 15x FY2027 consensus EPS of $4.10, with a forward PEG of 0.81, a 37% D/E, and an 11% free-cash-flow yield [3]. The Inspire score of 53 (ALIGNED) supports faith-based allocation.
thesis_continued: The bear case is that the recovery is narrow and early. TTM GAAP ROE is only 2.2% and net margin 1.9%, and Q1 2026 was still a loss [3]. LTL revenue excluding fuel grew only 0.4% in Q3, missing plan, and roughly half of the earnings beat reportedly came from gains on used-truck sales rather than core operations [2]. The dividend payout ratio of about 83% of TTM earnings leaves little cushion if freight weakens again, and the stock remains about 26% below its 52-week high of $82.86 [3].
key_catalysts: Truckload contract-rate resets in 2027 bid season, extending Q3's 9.7% rate-per-mile gain [1][2]
LTL network density improving operating ratio at AAA Cooper and MME as volumes recover [2]
FY2027 consensus EPS of $4.10, a roughly 70% increase over FY2026 consensus of $2.39, which would compress the P/E toward the low teens [3]
key_risks: Freight demand relapse driven by tariff or industrial weakness, reversing rate gains, with TTM net margin only 1.9% [3]
LTL underperformance, with Q3 revenue excluding fuel up only 0.4%, and a reliance on equipment-sale gains for earnings [2]
Insurance and claims costs plus wage-and-hour class actions [4][7]
